hint: A Python HTML sanitization library checks URI-valued attributes against a configurable scheme allowlist, then serializes the markup with character references left unresolved. An attacker controls the input markup and can place numeric or named character references in link, media, form and SVG attributes. The sanitizer must remove any attribute whose value resolves to a disallowed scheme after HTML entity resolution, while preserving the serialized bytes of allowed, relative and custom-protocol values.
surface: Python library made of a streaming HTML tokenizer, an attribute policy filter and an entity-preserving serializer. Untrusted markup enters through a sanitize API configured with allowed tags, allowed attributes and allowed URI schemes.
assumptions: The attacker controls the entire untrusted HTML fragment but not the sanitizer configuration or the local filesystem.
Allowed attributes include at least one URI-valued attribute on a link, an image, a video poster, a form action, a cite/background attribute and an SVG link.
The sanitizer's protocol list is configurable; http, https and mailto are allowed by default and a caller may add a custom scheme.
All experiments use a disposable local Python environment and in-memory strings; no network service or public target is involved.
The official benchmark evaluator is external; local test results are not an official pass.
